ui_bugs.issue: First click on ambiance-toggle-btn immediately after login-guest-btn is still lost. touchedRef via useRef is NOT persistent across React 18 StrictMode double-mount: the FIRST mount's prefsApi.get() closure captures a stale touchedRef that never becomes true, so when its promise resolves it can overwrite the user's theme choice (or the click closure of Header uses stale isDark). Observed: click1 no-op, click2 flips, click3 flips back. Test isolated: waited 4s after cockpit render before click #1 to let prefs settle; still fails.

action_items:
MEDIUM: Fix the first-click theme toggle race properly. Suggested approaches (any one):
  (a) Move `touchedRef` OUT of the component into a module-level `let touched = false;` so StrictMode's double-mount doesn't create two separate refs.
  (b) In Header.jsx toggleTheme, use functional setter that computes the next theme from the current prefs rather than reading isDark from the closure: e.g. expose setPref((prev)=>({...prev, theme: prev.theme==='light'?'dark':'light'})) via PrefsContext.
  (c) In PrefsContext useEffect, guard against overwriting theme once the effect from the first (unmounted) StrictMode pass resolves — use an AbortController or track a monotonically-increasing mount id.
  (d) Do not send theme in the prefsApi.get() overwrite path if theme was already patched (skip theme key when merging server response if we've already written it locally).
critical_code_review_comments: PrefsContext.jsx: useRef inside PrefsProvider does not survive StrictMode double-mount — each instance gets a fresh ref. Prefer a module-level flag or lift touchedRef via useRef(false) that reads from a singleton mounted at module scope.
Header.jsx toggleTheme reads `isDark` from render closure — could go stale under rapid state changes. Prefer functional patch pattern (setPref((prev)=>...)).

Onboarding.jsx still 697 lines, 15+ screens in a single component with an ad-hoc stepMeta dictionary — the fallback `|| { tag:'', n:99 }` prevents crashes but is a smell; consider deriving stepMeta from a single ordered array of screen definitions.

Focus retest on the theme toggle first-click after guest login: (1) go to /, (2) click login-guest-btn, (3) wait for ambiance-toggle-btn to appear + wait 3s, (4) assert document.documentElement.classList.contains('dark')===true, (5) click ambiance-toggle-btn ONCE, (6) after 500ms assert document.documentElement.classList.contains('dark')===false. The touchedRef-in-useRef approach does not survive StrictMode double-mount; move it to a module-level variable or refactor toggleTheme to use a functional setter.
rca of the issue: React 18 StrictMode invokes component effects twice (mount → unmount → remount). useRef(false) creates a fresh ref on each mount. The FIRST mount's useEffect fires prefsApi.get(); by the time this promise resolves, the component has been unmounted and remounted, so the second mount holds a different touchedRef. The first promise's closure still references the FIRST touchedRef, which is never set to true (because setPref runs on the second mount and only sets the SECOND touchedRef.current = true). Consequently when the first mount's promise resolves it passes the `if (touchedRef.current) return;` guard and calls setPrefs, overwriting the user's just-clicked theme back to the server value. Reproduction: 1) fresh page, 2) login-guest-btn, 3) wait for cockpit, 4) click ambiance-toggle-btn once → dark stays true. Mitigation: lift `touched` to module scope (`let TOUCHED = false;` outside the component), or use a functional-patch toggleTheme, or ignore `theme` key in the server-response merge whenever local setPrefs has already fired for theme.
